items.title: Google Removes JavaScript SEO Warning, Says It's Outdated
items.summary: Google has removed its outdated JavaScript SEO warning, which previously cautioned about designing for non-JavaScript environments, indicating that Search has rendered JavaScript effectively for years and that assistive technologies now support it. This change reduces concerns for SEO professionals relying on JavaScript for content loading, as Google emphasizes specific technical guidance over former broad advisories. However, site owners should still monitor JavaScript-heavy pages using tools like Search Console's URL Inspection, since other crawlers may not render JavaScript the same way.

items.title: New Google help document says frequent crawling is a good sign
items.summary: Google's new help document emphasizes that frequent crawling signals fresh, relevant content, which is crucial for SEO as it helps sites achieve better visibility in search results by meeting user demand. This reinforces the importance of maintaining up-to-date content, such as in ecommerce, to encourage more crawls and improve indexing. Site owners can leverage this by ensuring crawlability through tools and controls outlined in the document to enhance overall search performance.

items.title: Google AI Mode updates recipe results to better connect people with recipe creators
items.summary: Google's update to AI Mode enhances recipe search results by incorporating direct links to recipe sites and additional details like cook times, which could drive more referral traffic to content creators' websites from AI-generated overviews. This addresses ongoing issues where AI experiences previously failed to send sufficient traffic compared to traditional search results, potentially improving SEO for recipe bloggers through better visibility and click-through opportunities. However, the effectiveness in reducing 'AI slop' and boosting overall traffic remains uncertain pending further updates.

items.title: How the DOM affects crawling, rendering, and indexing
items.summary: The DOM significantly impacts SEO because Googlebot relies on the rendered DOM for crawling, rendering, and indexing, meaning JavaScript-dependent content must be present in the initial DOM to be visible and indexable, avoiding issues like crawl dead ends from non-standard links. Optimizing the DOM with semantic structures, proper link tags, and lean node counts enhances crawlability and performance metrics such as Core Web Vitals, while tools like URL Inspection help diagnose indexing problems. As AI agents increasingly interact with websites, a well-structured DOM will be crucial for future SEO and task completion.

items.title: Publishers Association says AI copyright exception calls are redundant
items.summary: The UK Publishers Association's study concludes that a growing licensing market for generative AI makes calls for a broad copyright exception unnecessary. Publishers have been actively licensing content for AI training, fostering a robust market. The report highlights the sector's adaptation to AI technologies through commercial agreements.

items.title: Publishing Ethics Clash With AI Book Flood On Kindle
items.summary: AI-generated books are flooding Amazon's Kindle store with low-cost, repetitive titles in genres like herbal remedies and romance, with 82% flagged as AI by detection tools. This influx raises ethical issues around originality, misinformation, and impersonation, while impacting authors' royalties and visibility. Amazon's policies require AI disclosure but lack consumer-facing labels, sparking calls for better transparency.

items.title: Sarah J Maas’s Past Controversy Resurfaces Amid New Book Buzz
items.summary: Sarah J. Maas announced two new ACOTAR books for late 2026 and early 2027 on the Call Her Daddy podcast, exciting BookTok and romantasy fans awaiting sequels since 2021. The buzz has reignited past criticisms over representation of marginalized characters and a 2020 promotional post amid Breonna Taylor discussions. Online debates continue on platforms like Threads regarding these issues and Maas's mental health disclosures.

items.title: JW Radford Signs Three-Book Publishing Deal with Poppy Grace Publishing
items.summary: Author JW Radford has signed a three-book deal with Poppy Grace Publishing, expanding on his themes of personal development, leadership, resilience, and purpose-driven success. The books will cover discipline, mindset, legacy, and overcoming adversity, drawing from his experiences as a business leader. The first title is slated for late February release, with more to follow.

items.title: PHC supporters David Shedd and Don Hodel release new books
items.summary: Patrick Henry College supporters David Shedd and Don Hodel have released new books: Shedd's 'The Great Heist' details China's espionage against Western tech and defense. Hodel's autobiography 'Called to Serve' recounts his Reagan Cabinet roles and public service alongside his late wife. Both works highlight national security and conservative leadership perspectives.

items.title: Paramount/Skydance to Acquire Warner Bros. Discovery
items.summary: David Ellison's Skydance and Paramount have agreed to buy Warner Bros. Discovery in a sweeping deal that promises to reinvent the studio's business. The acquisition includes commitments to keep CNN editorially independent. This merger marks a significant consolidation in the entertainment industry.

items.title: Netflix Acquires Ben Affleck's AI Filmmaking Startup
items.summary: Netflix has acquired InterPositive, an AI-powered filmmaking tools startup founded by Ben Affleck, who will advise the streamer. The deal underscores the increasing role of artificial intelligence in content creation. Financial terms were not disclosed.

items.title: Oscars 2026 Announces Star-Studded Presenters Lineup
items.summary: Anne Hathaway, Paul Mescal, Robert Downey Jr., and more have been named as presenters for the 2026 Academy Awards. The lineup adds glamour to the ceremony. Further announcements are anticipated.

items.title: Scary Movie Sequel Trailer Draws Backlash Over Pronoun Joke
items.summary: The trailer for Scary Movie 6 features a joke about pronouns in its opening subway stabbing scene, sparking outrage from some viewers who deemed it offensive. Supporters argue it aligns with the series' tradition of irreverent satire. Reactions on social media are sharply divided.

items.title: Scream 7 Star Anna Camp Faces Backlash, Apologizes for Boycott Post
items.summary: Anna Camp deleted an Instagram post celebrating Scream 7's box office prospects despite boycott calls from pro-Palestine activists and issued an apology. Critics accused her of insensitivity amid the film's controversies. The movie continues toward a potential franchise record opening.

items.title: The White Lotus Season 4 Adds Vincent Cassel and More to Cast
items.summary: French actors Vincent Cassel, Corentin Fila, and Nadia Tereszkiewicz join the cast of HBO's The White Lotus Season 4. The anthology series maintains its appeal with international talent. Production details are forthcoming.

items.title: Launch Commerce Rebrands from Launch Cart, Unveils AI-Powered Business Platform for Small Businesses
items.summary: Launch Commerce, formerly Launch Cart, has launched an AI-powered platform featuring seven integrated products like Launch AI Workforce for 24/7 lead qualification and booking, Launch CRM for automated follow-ups, and Launch Ads for managing ads across 11 platforms. Designed for small and mid-sized businesses such as HVAC firms and law offices, it consolidates tools into one system to automate operations, capture leads faster, and boost revenue. The platform was announced on March 4, 2026, as part of their 2026 growth strategy.

items.title: How NYC Small Businesses Are Putting AI to Work for Them
items.summary: NYC small businesses and nonprofits are using AI to boost efficiency without job cuts, via programs like Tech to Table and Decoded Futures. Examples include a Korean restaurant employing AI for menu checks, customer queries, and multilingual HR, while Welcome to Chinatown uses Claude for surveys and event management, slashing task times dramatically. Another startup, Cai.audio, aids musicians with AI for note adjustments and anti-theft tools, showing practical AI adoption.

items.title: Why Claude Sonnet 4.6 Is A Major AI Upgrade For Small Businesses
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6 offers a 1M-token context window for handling large documents, superior instruction-following, and accuracy gains, available affordably via Amazon Bedrock and GitHub Copilot. It enables small businesses to automate workflows, generate code, and analyze data without AI teams, cutting costs and speeding product delivery. Published February 26, 2026, it promises ROI through efficiency in reports, decisions, and operations.

items.title: Intuit Partners with Anthropic to Integrate Custom AI Agents for Businesses
items.summary: Intuit and Anthropic have partnered to embed Claude Agent SDK into Intuit's platform, allowing mid-market businesses to create secure AI agents for tasks like accounting and payroll in industries such as construction and healthcare. It also brings Intuit's financial expertise to Claude users for seamless execution. Rollout starts spring 2026, as reported February 28.

items.title: How To Use Claude Cowork To Run Your Business With AI
items.summary: Claude Cowork, an AI agent in the Claude app, automates business tasks like document analysis, research, and report building by accessing folders and running parallel threads. Founders can set it up on Pro plan to categorize data, compare options, or prototype, freeing time for strategy. Examples include podcast insights and supplier evaluation, dated February 24, 2026.
